questions.q: What does `contract ERC20Test is ERC20 { }` actually do?
options: Deletes OpenZeppelin's ERC20 contract
Only imports the ERC20 contract's variable names, not its functions
Uses real Solidity inheritance so ERC20Test automatically gets every function OpenZeppelin's ERC20 defines
Creates a completely empty contract with no functions at all
questions.explain: The `is ERC20` syntax is real inheritance — the new contract automatically inherits transfer, approve, transferFrom, and everything else ERC20 implements.

questions.q: Where did the instructor find the real ERC20 contract to import?
options: Ethereum's own official website
A random pastebin link
It was already built into Remix by default
OpenZeppelin's own GitHub repository, under contracts/token/ERC20
questions.explain: The real, audited ERC20.sol lives in OpenZeppelin's GitHub repo, under contracts/token/ERC20 — the instructor navigated there directly and copied the file's URL.

questions.q: Why do real production tokens generally prefer OpenZeppelin's ERC20 over a hand-written version?
options: OpenZeppelin's version has already been reviewed by security researchers, reducing real risk
OpenZeppelin's contracts cannot be imported into Remix
Hand-written versions are always faster to deploy
There's no real difference in practice
questions.explain: Reusing an already-audited, widely-used implementation avoids the real risk of reintroducing bugs that a from-scratch implementation might contain.

questions.q: What real value does writing your own ERC-20 by hand (from the previous lessons) still provide, per this lesson?
options: It replaces the need to ever read documentation
It has no value at all once OpenZeppelin exists
It's required before OpenZeppelin's contracts can even compile
It builds a genuine understanding of how the mechanics actually work, even if you use OpenZeppelin's version in production
questions.explain: Understanding the real mechanics — balances, allowances, events — makes it possible to actually reason about and extend a production-grade implementation later.

questions.q: What does importing a contract directly by its GitHub URL, as shown in this lesson, actually require?
options: Pasting the file's real raw GitHub URL inside the import statement's quotes
Manually retyping the entire contract by hand
Downloading and re-uploading the file first
A special paid Remix plugin
questions.explain: Just like the earlier OpenZeppelin lesson in Chapter 7, pasting a file's GitHub URL directly into an import statement pulls the real, live source in without retyping it.
